output:
## Overview

Your chart is built around a Life Palace in Zi 子 that holds Lian Zhen (the principled, socially sharp observer who likes to see how things really work) at fair brightness together with Tian Xiang (the composed administrator, the one who keeps order and keeps promises), the latter at brilliant brightness. The Body Palace also falls in Zi, in the same Life Palace, which is unusual and telling: your outer life and your inner life pull in the same direction, so what you show the world tends to be genuinely you rather than a mask. The Five Element Bureau is Wood 3, a quick, growing, idea-fertile rhythm that suits learning, adapting and starting things more than digging into one long slow trench.

For a newcomer: the twelve palaces are twelve life areas arranged in a wheel, and each one holds stars that colour it. The Life Palace is the core self — temperament, instinct, the way you meet the world. The Body Palace shows where the body and the lived life actually go, the part of you that acts. When both land in the same palace, character and conduct are closely bound together.

The two most distinctive traits here are a strong sense of order paired with a very visible presence. Tian Xiang wants fairness and clean structure; Lian Zhen wants to understand motives and can be both charming and exacting. Behind them sits Qi Sha (the disciplined general, the lone executor who moves when the moment is right) at brilliant brightness in the Wellbeing Palace, and Po Jun (the pioneer who clears the old to build the new) at brilliant brightness in the Travel Palace opposite you. So the mild, orderly exterior covers a decisive, renovating engine.

## Life Palace and Personality

Lian Zhen at fair brightness in the Life Palace gives you a mind that enjoys complexity — people, systems, power dynamics, the "why" behind behaviour. It can make you a superb reader of a room and also a demanding critic, of others and especially of yourself. Tian Xiang at brilliant brightness alongside it softens and steadies that: it adds a taste for dignity, a dislike of mess and unfairness, and a real capacity for administrative patience. The pairing reads as someone who looks diplomatic but has firm private standards, and who does best when those standards are spoken rather than swallowed.

Challenging support here is Qing Yang (the blunt blade, directness that cuts fast), which sits in your Life Palace. It sharpens decisiveness and honesty but can make your first reaction more confrontational than you intend. Channelled well, it is the part of you that says the necessary thing in a meeting when everyone else is hedging; channelled badly, it lands before you have chosen your words. A useful working habit is the deliberate pause — let the sharpness inform the message, then deliver it in Tian Xiang's measured tone.

Because the Body Palace shares this palace, your instincts and your actions stay consistent, which people tend to trust. The opposite palace, the Travel Palace, holds Po Jun at brilliant brightness, so the wider world, travel, new environments and public exposure all tend to pull the pioneer out of you. You are likely to grow fastest when you are not standing still.

## Career

The Career Palace in Chen 辰 holds Wu Qu (the steady builder, the one who values method, quality and a fair return) at brilliant brightness — and Wu Qu carries your birth-year Hua Ji (obstacle, where extra care is needed). This is a genuinely important detail: the palace of work is strong and capable, but the transformation there suggests friction, delay or a lesson in doing things properly rather than quickly. The friction tends to show up around perfectionism, unmet expectations, or tasks where you feel your effort is not matched by recognition. Working with it means building in review stages, documenting your process, and refusing to let one snag read as a verdict on your ability.

Wen Chang (the scholar-star of writing, structure and articulate presentation) sits in the same palace, which is excellent support: your credibility comes from clarity — writing, planning, explaining, teaching, drafting. Ling Xing (the quick spark, a sharp impatient energy) also sits here, and it is best treated as fuel rather than noise: it makes you fast under deadline, and it needs a routine that gives it somewhere to go. Combining Wu Qu's method with Wen Chang's expression suggests work where craft and communication meet — operations, editing, analysis, design, project leadership, technical writing, or building something to a standard you can defend.

The Career Palace's opposite is the Spouse Palace, holding Tan Lang at brilliant brightness, which links your professional style to your partnership life: a supportive partner tends to function as a sounding board for career decisions, and work stress that is not discussed at home tends to spill into the relationship.

## Wealth

This is one of the strongest parts of the chart. The Wealth Palace in Shen 申 holds Zi Wei (the emperor star, the one who leads, organizes and expects a certain standard) at bright brightness carrying your birth-year Hua Quan (power, the ability to take charge and be recognized for it), and Tian Fu (the treasurer, the steady keeper of resources) at steady brightness. Two things follow. First, you are naturally suited to managing resources rather than chasing them — budgeting, structuring, holding the centre while others scatter. Second, the Hua Quan here means your financial life tends to improve when you take visible responsibility: running the household economy, negotiating your own terms, or leading a project with a budget attached.

Zuo Fu (the helpful ally, loyal practical support) sits in this palace and itself carries Hua Ke (recognition, reputation, the reward of doing something well and being seen to do it well). That is a strong signal that steady, well-presented competence brings opportunities through people who trust your reliability. Huo Xing (the sudden flare, bursts of drive and impatience) also sits here, so the pattern worth watching is unevenness: bursts of energy followed by lulls. A simple rhythm of regular review, small consistent steps and a written plan tends to suit this palace far better than dramatic moves.

The opposite palace is the Wellbeing Palace with Qi Sha at brilliant brightness, which adds an edge of discipline to money: you are likely to do best with a system you actually follow, and less well with improvisation under pressure.

## Love and Partnership

The Spouse Palace in Xu 戌 holds Tan Lang at brilliant brightness — the star of attraction, sociability, appetite for experience and charm. This points to a partner who is expressive, magnetic and interesting, and to relationships that thrive on shared novelty rather than routine. It also suggests you yourself bring warmth and a certain sparkle to partnership when you feel free. Wen Qu (the graceful communicator, the one who writes and speaks with care) sits in this palace, which favours relationships built on good conversation and thoughtful gestures — notes, messages, and the small articulate things that show attention.

Tu Luo (the slow turn, delay and accumulated friction) also sits here. Present it honestly as a pace-setting factor: matters of the heart may take longer to develop, or a recurring point of friction may need patient, repeated conversation rather than one dramatic talk. That is the way to channel it — name the small issue early and calmly instead of letting it build. The link to the Career Palace opposite means career pressure and partnership are entangled; a season of overwork tends to register at home, so protecting time together is a practical form of care.

The Children Palace with Tai Yin at bright brightness sits in your current Major Period, which often brings themes of nurturing, home and younger people into the foreground — worth keeping in view when you think about the shape of your domestic life.

## Wellbeing Habits

The Health Palace in Wei 未 holds Tian Ji (the strategist, the restless thinker who plans and replans) at fallen brightness. In practice this tends to describe a mind that does not switch off easily: thinking in bed, replaying conversations, planning tomorrow during today. The Life Palace's Lian Zhen adds a habit of analyzing your own state, which can be useful but can also keep the loop running. The most valuable wellbeing habit for this configuration is a clear end-of-day boundary — writing tomorrow's list before you stop, so the strategist has somewhere to put its work.

Food and movement suit a regular, uncomplicated rhythm. Tian Ji's nature favours variety in ideas but not in meals; simple, repeated, well-timed eating tends to sit better than grazing while working. For movement, the Wood 3 Bureau and Qi Sha in the Wellbeing Palace favour something structured and slightly demanding — a class at a set time, a training plan with visible progress — rather than vague intentions. The Travel Palace's Po Jun at brilliant brightness also suggests you do well when movement takes you outdoors or somewhere new.

Emotionally, the pattern to watch is the critic in Lian Zhen turning inward. Qing Yang's bluntness in the Life Palace can make self-criticism unusually sharp. Give that energy an outlet — a journal, a trusted friend who will not just agree with you, or the discipline of writing out what is actually true rather than what feels urgent.

If you feel unwell, please consult a qualified healthcare professional.

## Family and Social Circle

The Friends Palace in Si 巳 holds Tai Yang (the sun, generosity, visibility, the one who warms a group) at bright brightness, supported by Tian Yue (the gentle benefactor, help that arrives through goodwill). This is a warm signature: your wider circle tends to include open, generous people who speak well of you, and your own sociability is genuine rather than tactical. It also means you are likely to be the one who connects others.

Two challenging stars sit here as well: Di Kong (the hollow, an emptiness that dissolves fixed expectations) and Di Jie (the barrier, a check that forces reconsideration). Read together, they suggest that some social plans and alliances will not materialize as hoped, and that a few connections will need more effort than they return. The useful framing is selectivity: Di Kong and Di Jie are good at showing you which relationships are real. Let them thin the circle rather than discourage you, and put your energy into the few friendships that survive a delay.

The Parents Palace in Chou 丑 holds Tian Liang (the elder, the mentor, the principled guide) at bright brightness carrying your birth-year Hua Lu (prosperity, ease and flow). That is a strong indication of supportive senior figures — parents, teachers, bosses, mentors — who open doors and smooth paths. It is worth actively maintaining those relationships; a short, regular check-in goes a long way. Tian Kui (the noble helper, timely assistance from above) sits in the Property Palace, reinforcing the theme of steady backing in matters of home and long-term security.

The Siblings Palace holds Ju Men at bright brightness (the debater, the one who argues a case), and in 2027 it takes a Hua Ji, so family-of-origin or sibling conversation is an area to approach with extra patience rather than point-scoring.

## Major Period and Year by Year

Your current Major Period runs from traditional age 33 to 42 and falls in the Children Palace in You 酉, which holds Tai Yin (the moon, nurture, sensitivity, the keeper of home and inner life) at bright brightness. Ten years with the moon in charge tend to be quieter in outer drama and deeper in inner life: focus gathers around home, close relationships, caregiving, creativity, and the patient building of something personal. The pace is more reflective than explosive, and the most rewarding move in these years is to give sustained attention to the things that grow slowly. The next Major Period, from age 43 to 52, moves into the Wealth Palace in Shen 申 with Zi Wei holding Hua Quan and Tian Fu alongside Zuo Fu carrying Hua Ke — a distinctly more public, resourceful, leadership-flavoured decade, where the foundations built now would be asked to carry real weight.

The annual pillars below follow the Chinese lunar year, so each one roughly matches the calendar year but starts at the lunar new year rather than at the start of the calendar year.

### 2026 丙午 · Bing Wu

The annual Life Palace falls in the Travel Palace in Wu 午, home to Po Jun at brilliant brightness, so this year's tone is renovation and movement: changing environments, breaking an old pattern, being seen in unfamiliar settings. Bing Wu's transformations put Hua Lu on Tian Tong in the Property Palace — an easier, more comfortable feel around home and living arrangements, a good time to settle or improve your space. Hua Quan on Tian Ji in the Health Palace favours taking deliberate charge of your daily routine. Hua Ke on Wen Chang in the Career Palace rewards anything written, presented or documented; this is a good time to put your work into words. Hua Ji lands on Lian Zhen in the Life Palace, which asks for care with self-criticism and with sharp remarks made under pressure. Lean into the Po Jun momentum early in the year and keep the inner critic on a shorter leash toward the end of the year.

### 2027 丁未 · Ding Wei

The annual Life Palace moves into the Health Palace in Wei 未 with Tian Ji at fallen brightness, a year where the strategist runs the show — lots of planning, adjusting, re-planning. Ding Wei brings Hua Lu to Tai Yin in the Children Palace, which is a gentle, nurturing influence on home and creative projects; the first half of the year is well suited to putting time into those. Hua Quan on Tian Tong in the Property Palace again favours taking decisions about your living situation rather than drifting. Hua Ke on Tian Ji in the Health Palace supports small, practical improvements to routine. Hua Ji falls on Ju Men in the Siblings Palace, so conversations with siblings or old family arguments may need a slower pace and more listening than debating. Overall this is a year for patient consolidation rather than big launches.

### 2028 戊申 · Wu Shen

The annual Life Palace lands in the Wealth Palace in Shen 申, with Zi Wei carrying Hua Quan and Tian Fu at steady brightness, alongside Zuo Fu and Huo Xing — a year with real momentum behind practical resource management and visible responsibility. Wu Shen puts Hua Lu on Tan Lang in the Spouse Palace, which tends to warm partnership and social life; it is a good year for shared plans and enjoyment. Hua Quan on Tai Yin in the Children Palace supports taking charge of home and nurturing matters. Hua Ke on You Bi in the Travel Palace brings helpful people through travel and outside connections. Hua Ji falls on Tian Ji in the Health Palace, which flags the restless-mind theme: the risk this year is overthinking, so build in genuine breaks rather than pushing through. Lean into the Wealth Palace confidence in the first half and guard your rest in the second half.

### 2029 己酉 · Ji You

The annual Life Palace returns to the Children Palace in You 酉, Tai Yin at bright brightness — the same palace as your ten-year Major Period, so this year tends to bring the decade's themes to a head. Ji You puts Hua Lu on Wu Qu in the Career Palace, a strong and welcome turn for work: method is rewarded, and effort is more likely to be noticed. Hua Quan on Tan Lang in the Spouse Palace favours taking the lead in partnership decisions. Hua Ke on Tian Liang in the Parents Palace brings recognition or support from senior figures — a good time to ask for guidance or a reference. Hua Ji lands on Wen Qu in the Spouse Palace, so careful wording matters in close relationships; a message sent in haste could be read too sharply. Put real energy into career in the first half of the year, and slow your communication down toward the end.

### 2030 庚戌 · Geng Xu

The annual Life Palace moves into the Spouse Palace in Xu 戌, with Tan Lang at brilliant brightness and both Wen Qu and Tuo Luo for company — a year where partnership, close friendship and how you communicate take centre stage. Geng Xu puts Hua Lu on Tai Yang in the Friends Palace, which is excellent for your network: people are warm, introductions go well, and collaboration tends to be generous in spirit. Hua Quan on Wu Qu in the Career Palace again rewards taking visible responsibility at work, and Hua Ke on Tai Yin in the Children Palace supports home and creative matters. Hua Ji falls on Tian Tong in the Property Palace, so property, living arrangements or family comfort may feel sticky — better to plan carefully than to improvise. This is a good year to lean on your circle in spring and summer, and to keep home decisions considered in autumn and winter.

## Guidance

- **Use Wen Chang in the Career Palace deliberately.** Whatever your field, put your thinking into written form — proposals, documentation, a personal project you publish. Wu Qu's Hua Ji in the same palace eases when your process is visible and well organized, so build review steps into how you work rather than trusting speed alone.
- **Keep the Life Palace's Qing Yang on a short leash.** Before sending a sharp message or making a blunt remark, wait an hour and rewrite it in Tian Xiang's measured tone. The directness is an asset; the timing is the variable you can control.
- **Make your Wealth Palace structure explicit.** With Zi Wei's Hua Quan, Tian Fu, Zuo Fu and Hua Ke all here, a written monthly review of income and spending suits you far better than an improvised approach, and it fits Huo Xing's tendency toward uneven energy.
- **Schedule rest as part of the plan.** Tian Ji at fallen brightness in the Health Palace, reinforced by its Hua Ji in 2028 and 2030, points to a mind that will not stop on its own. A fixed wind-down routine and tomorrow's list written before you stop is the single most useful habit from this chart.
- **Tend the Parents Palace.** Tian Liang carries your birth-year Hua Lu there, so mentors and senior figures are among your best resources. A short, regular check-in with one or two such people keeps that flow alive and can open doors in the Wealth-focused decade ahead.
